scenario.label: Who actually carried the launch
scenario.brief: We shipped the new onboarding flow last week and it went well. Before we do the all-hands I want to know who actually did what, in their own words, because the people who present are not always the people who did the work.
scenario.theDecision: The designer is the one everybody credits and she credits somebody else - a contractor who built the migration script over a weekend and is not on the team. A right answer surfaces the uncredited contributor by name, from the others' accounts rather than from his own.

people.name: Laura Whitfield
people.truth: She thinks the launch went well because of the design work. She does not know a migration script existed. She is planning to name the designer and the two engineers at the all-hands.
people.manner: Generous with praise, a bit high-level. Gets specific when asked who did which part.

people.name: Amara Diallo
people.remit: Product designer. Did the flow design.
people.truth: Her design work was two weeks and fine. The thing that made the launch work was Victor's migration script, which moved 60,000 existing users onto the new flow without anybody noticing. He is a contractor, finished on Friday, and is not in the all-hands. She will say this if asked who else was involved.
people.manner: Modest, deflects praise, precise about what she did and did not do.

people.name: Joseph Mwangi
people.truth: He built the front end. He also thinks Victor's script was the hard part and that Victor worked the weekend of the 14th to do it. He assumed somebody had told the PM.

All three people have answered. You describe coordinating the vision for the new onboarding flow, while Amara Diallo and Joseph Mwangi both say a script from somebody named Victor was the critical part of the work.
